Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, Mediva is moving a POC for an isolated/regulatory workload next quarter and we need a clear sizing recommendation so procurement can scope the SOW. A few constraints and numbers from our side:

- Estimated steady-state concurrent requests: 120 QPS (text generation path, typical prompt length ~250 tokens)
- Peak bursts: up to 300 QPS sustained for short windows (~20-30 minutes) during clinician shift changes
- Models: LLM-Redwood-7B (baseline) and LLM-Redwood-13B for higher-quality routing
- Data residency: US-only (patient PHI), SOC2 + HIPAA requirements — compliance team will request evidence
- Desired SLA: 99.9% availability, p95 latency target <= 200ms for baseline model

Can you send a short breakdown comparing: (A) private deployment footprint (VPC/on-prem-ish) vs (B) dedicated reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated)? We need predicted GPU counts, recommended tiling (multi-model host layout), rough monthly cost bands, and recovery/fallback paths if we hit peaks. Procurement wants a quick summary they can include in the SOW.

I've CC'd procurement (procurement@mediva.com) and compliance so they see the ask.

Cheers,
Alice

Alice — thanks for the clear inputs. Attaching a quick spreadsheet (sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx) with two scenario sketches and the assumptions. High level summary below; I looped in Kar/Marissa/Jonas for technical and rollout notes.

Executive summary (short):
- Private (Redwood Private) — best for strict data control and auditability. Expect higher up-front engineering time and a minimum committed footprint (we typically recommend a 2N design for availability). For your load profile: ~10–14 A100-equivalent GPUs (multi-tenant within your VPC) to hit p95 targets with headroom; more if you want heavier model (13B) on dedicated hosts.
- Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated Reserved Capacity) — faster to stand up, lower operational lift from Mediva. For same SLA and headroom: ~8–10 A100-equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool with autoscaling bursts to a shared overflow fleet for short peaks. Cost is generally lower monthly but less isolation.

Key trade-offs (short):
- Isolation vs economics: Private = highest isolation, higher cost and lead time. Dedicated = strong economics, simpler procurement.
- Peak handling: Dedicated + burst autoscale can be cheaper if you accept routed bursts to a lower-tier pool; Private requires committed extra capacity or a hybrid burst path (e.g., private primary + dedicated overflow).
- Compliance evidence: Private gives clearer audit boundary (customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM). We can still provide SOC2 artifacts and attestations for Dedicated but some customers prefer Private to avoid shared tenancy questions.

Next steps I propose: Kar provides a model-by-model GPU tiling and cost delta (tomorrow), Marissa to outline rollout & canary, Jonas to confirm latency and kernel-optimization assumptions. I'll produce a mutual action plan for procurement once we align on counts.

Attachments: sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx

Best,

Alice, Tessa — ran a quick sizing pass with Jonas's perf profiles and the team's historical telemetry. Attaching a more granular model (sizing_model_v2.xlsx) with per-model tiling and latency band projections. Highlights below — numbers are A100-equivalent GPU counts and back-of-envelope monthly OPEX (USD).

Assumptions (short):
- Baseline model (7B) throughput: ~55 tokens/ms per GPU for 250-token prompts with Redwood attention optimizations
- 13B model throughput: ~30 tokens/ms per GPU
- Average tokens per response ~450 (includes prompt + generation)
- Safety margin: 1.5x steady-state to smooth scheduling and KV cache warmup

A) Private (customer-managed VPC):
- Baseline (primary on 7B): 8 GPUs for steady-state, 16 GPUs for 2N high-availability (recommended). If you want both 7B and 13B resident: 22 GPUs (split tiling to keep p95 <200ms).
- Peak plan: cross-region cold standby and on-demand burst to dedicated pool via secured peering (adds ~4–6 GPUs on demand).
- Monthly OPEX estimate (incl. support & license): $145k–$210k (depends on commit term and telemetry retention).

B) Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated reserved pool):
- Recommended reserved: 10 GPUs committed (mix of smaller cards aggregated) with autoscale policy to 18 GPUs for short bursts. We route overflow to a shared high-capacity cluster if peaks exceed committed + burst (we throttle non-critical lower-priority requests).
- Monthly OPEX estimate: $115k–$160k (includes reserved discount).

Operational and procurement notes:
- Private rollout lead time: 6–10 weeks for infra and HSM/KMS integration + security reviews. Dedicated: 1–2 weeks for reserved capacity provisioning.
- Fallback: Recommend hybrid MAP — Private primary + Dedicated overflow to avoid overprovisioning while retaining strong isolation for PHI paths.

I'll be available for a technical call with your infra/security team — proposed times below.

Attachments: sizing_model_v2.xlsx

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Procurement / Alice — following up with a concise mutual action plan and the pricing anchors you asked for. I've also left in-line answers to your two points below.

In-line:
> 1) If we choose Private with 2N (16 GPUs), can Redwood provide a firm uplift price for converting to Dedicated overflow (e.g., per-hour rate for bursts)?

Yes — we can lock an overflow hourly uplift rate tied to your commit tier for the POC term. Example anchor: $32/hour per A100-eq GPU for overflow when routed from private to Redwood Dedicated (with a monthly cap negotiated). I'll put a formal uplift table into the SOW.

> 2) If we go Dedicated reserved at 10 GPUs with burst to 18, what are the SLA credits and penalties if p95 or availability targets are missed during bursts?

SLA notes: Reserved capacity includes a 99.9% availability guarantee. If we miss availability targets for Reserved + Burst window attributable to Redwood control plane, standard SLA credits apply (per contract). For p95 latency misses specifically during bursts where overflow routing is used, we propose a remedial plan (priority routing adjustment + engineering post-mortem) and a credit banding: 5% credit for single-day regressions, escalating for repeated breaches. We can draft exact credit language for legal.

Mutual action plan (MAP) — timeline (decision target 2027-05-18):
- 2027-05-12: Alignment on counts and MAP (this email) — deliverables: finalized GPU counts, preferred hosting mode (Private / Dedicated / Hybrid)
- 2027-05-14: Security artifacts & preliminary SOW draft (Redwood delivers SOC2 package, network diagram, KMS notes) — action: Redwood (Marissa + Jonas)
- 2027-05-16: Pricing & MAP finalization (Redwood to populate SOW with uplift table and SLAs) — action: Tessa / Finance
- 2027-05-18: Decision and signature (Mediva) — action: Mediva Procurement / Legal

Proposed recommended configuration (our read based on perf and headroom):
- Hybrid mode (recommended for POC): Private primary with 2N baseline for PHI-critical routes (16 GPUs), Dedicated reserved overlay at 10 GPUs with autoscale to 18 for non-PHI or overflow during peak windows. This minimizes upfront capex/time while ensuring PHI stays within your VPC.

Attachments provided: redwood-multipath-ma-poc.docx, docusign-mutual-action-plan-link.txt (DocuSign MAP link)

Next steps: Alice — can you confirm the internal sign-off path and whether legal needs a separate DPA? If procurement is happy, I'll engage Finance and Legal and drop a formal SOW draft by Friday.

Thanks all — available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow to run through the MAP.

Best,
